title: Asymptotic ladder deployment notebook (staging -> canary)
content:
Purpose: quick personal ledger for an "asymptotic ladder" staged rollout from internal staging to small external canary. Goal = smooth ramp while preserving latency budget and minimizing wasted capacity. This is a raw scratchpad — runbook snippets, open questions, TODOs, and quick commands.

High-level idea (one-liner): instead of fixed percent gates, use discrete 'ladder rungs' with dwell times and queue-weighted spillover. Rungs: 0% -> 0.1% -> 0.5% -> 1% -> 3% -> 7% -> 15% (stop/rollback on hit). Each rung has minimum dwell (15m) + telemetry pass.

Key constraints and assumptions:
- Target model: rtx-alpha-v2 pinned in staging image (digest=sha256:9d3a)
- Latency SLO (p95) <= 220ms for text-gen (seq=256); error rate target < 0.5% 5m rolling
- Capacity: Dedicated pool can absorb up to 50 concurrent long requests, usual warmpool=10
- Telemetry channels: #sre-rollouts (slack), prod-alerts, datadog-dashboard:serving/rollouts/asymptote

Pre-roll checklist (things I want done before waving traffic):
- [ ] confirm image digest pinned in release manifest and SDK toggle default (manifest: release/2026-03-10-alpha)
- [ ] create canary cohort tag in routing config: cohort=asymptote-zane
- [ ] warm KV-cache on 3 warmup clients (see warmup commands below)
- [ ] run smoke test suite against staging pinned instance (smoke-suite/release-quick)
- [ ] update rollout Jira RW-2409 with today's plan and point-at PR #812

Warmup commands (ad-hoc):
- curl http://staging-inference.internal/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"rtx-alpha-v2","prompt":"warmup token seq 1"}'
- run 50 short sequences (len 64) from warmup-scripts/warm-primers.py (parallel=3)
- verify KV cache filling: datadog check "kv_cache_hit_rate" -> expect > 60% after warmup

Telemetry pass checklist per rung (must pass all):
- p95 latency <= 220ms over the last 15m (for rung dwell)
- errors <= 0.5% (5m rolling)
- CPU/GPU utilization within safe range (GPU <= 82% sustained)
- no new exception classes in logs (grep for stack traces)
- no model-quality alarms (eval drift monitor unchanged)

Rung dwell logic (notes):
- dwell = max(15m, 3x median completion time). If any threshold violated escalate immediately and pin traffic back to previous rung.
- automatic backoff: if latency or errors spike then reduce by 50% of current rung traffic and re-evaluate after 10m. Manual rollback if >2 threshold hits.

Quick rollout sequence (live commands & checks):
1) push manifest with cohort tag and pinned digest -> deploy to standby staging nodes
2) run warmup commands against staging nodes (10m)
3) shift 0.1% traffic via routing API:
   - curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/routing/update -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP' -d '{"cohort":"asymptote-zane","percent":0.1,"priority":"low"}'
4) monitor telemetry for 15m (use datadog dashboard bookmark and slack alert rules)
5) if pass -> advance to 0.5% after dwell; else rollback to 0% and mark incident in RW-2409

Rollback & escape hatch notes:
- Immediate: curl to set cohort percent=0.0 and re-route to previous stable model
- If route API fails, use k8s patch to scale down canary deployment replicas to 0
- If autoscaler misbehaves, activate capacity-throttle policy in dedicated pool (Ops runbook step 4)

Soft-fallback strategy (for degraded model quality):
- Use routing policy that can route to a lower-capacity but higher-quality variant (rtx-alpha-v1-quant) for 20% of failed queries (via header-based routing).
- Add a reranking step in client SDK to prefer older model when model-quality score < 0.7 (temporary until fix)

Observability anchors to watch in the first 60 minutes:
- datadog: serving.requests.count, serving.requests.errors, serving.latency.p95, kv_cache_hit_rate, gpu.utilization
- logs: fastgrep for "NullPointer" or "bad_tokenization" occurrences
- eval harness: run 100 golden prompts against canary every 5m and verify AA score > baseline -2%

Open questions / TODOs (personal):
- [ ] confirm whether dedicated pool autoscaler respects per-cohort soft quotas (Harper to confirm)
- [ ] add a lightweight synthetic traffic generator as a console job (low-cost) so we can continuously warm caches pre-roll
- [ ] do we want to expose a per-customer emergency pin toggle (API present but needs ACL review)
- [ ] define SLA note for this canary (do we declare it 'experimental' in dashboard?)

Post-roll actions (if successful):
- document exact times and rung transitions in RW-2409 with short notes (timestamps + rationale)
- flip canary cohort to 'monitored' and add to daily ingestion for one week
- schedule a short retro with SRE + product owners: 30m standup within 48h

Quick command snippets for on-call (keep handy):
- set cohort traffic to 0%: curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/routing/update -d '{"cohort":"asymptote-zane","percent":0.0}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP'
- scale down k8s: kubectl -n serving rollout pause deployment/rtx-alpha-v2-canary; kubectl scale deploy rtx-alpha-v2-canary --replicas=0
- revert to pinned stable model: POST /deployments/rollback {"service":"serving","to_tag":"stable-202602"}

Notes to self (fragments):
- keep rung progression conservative; avoid gang-of-1 decisions unless urgent
- the ladder metaphor helps explain to PMs: each rung buys time and telemetry, not just a percent flip
- consider adding a 'safety corridor' where we temporarily divert non-critical long-seq requests during middle rungs

Finish: save this as a sketch, push selected items to RW-2409 checklist, ping @Maya for final signoff before staging warmup.
notes_summary: Scratchpad for an "asymptotic ladder" deployment plan: runged percent increases, telemetry gates, warmup commands, rollback & fallback strategies, and open questions. For eng-serving-runtime personal use.
